presentation.description: Finds something in your saved history by what it MEANS, not just by the words you use. Word-based lookup matches words: ask about "running something on a timer" and a conversation that said "cron job" is not found at all. Meaning-based recall also lets the engine ask "have we been here before?" and get answers worded differently from the question — the case where it would otherwise repeat a decision you already made. It is a required part of memory: every memory read can use it, and it reads only, never changing or removing anything you have saved. What it carries, plainly: a language table of about 33 MB committed with the engine, so nothing is downloaded when you use it; one ordinary Python package (numpy) that setting the engine up fetches over the network, like the engine's other tools; and a working copy built alongside your saved history the first time a meaning question is asked, taking a few seconds and roughly two to four times the size of that history.
